title: Intel once shipped a chip that divided wrongly
body: In 1994 a mathematics professor found that Pentium chips returned wrong results for certain divisions. Five entries were missing from a lookup table in the floating-point unit, making rare divisions slightly inaccurate. Intel first downplayed, then replaced chips, taking a charge of about 475 million dollars.
source_hint: Intel FDIV erratum and 1994 recall records
